full_text:
The 2026 NFL season is just around the corner, which means more NFL player props are being released with each passing week. I previously broke down the [2026 NFL Receiving Yards Props](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-player-props-receiving-yards), and it’s time to dive into the 2026 NFL Receiving Yards Leader odds for the top wide receivers and tight ends. In this article, I highlighted a bet I’ve already dropped in our Betting Discord and a couple of additional wagers I considered.

__Jaxon Smith-Njigba__ cashed the 12th-longest odds at +3000 with an NFL-best 1793 yards last season. He beat out __Puka Nacua__ (1715, +1500) for the honor, as no other receiver even reached 1430+ receiving yards in 2025. Nacua is the favorite to lead the league in receiving yards this season at +550 odds. He’s followed closely by top contenders like JSN (+650), __Ja’Marr Chase__ (+650), __Amon-Ra St. Brown__ (+1000), and __CeeDee Lamb__ (+1200) at 12/1 odds or shorter.

\>Be sure to check out [Brolley’s Best Bets: 2026 NFL Futures](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/series/2025/best-bets) for my favorite futures bets all offseason…Subscribe to the Best Bets Podcast on your [favorite platform](https://www.fantasypoints.com/media/podcasts/show/nfl-best-bets) and on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@FantasyPointsBetting) for year-round NFL betting talk…Join our “futures-betting” [Fantasy Points Discord](https://www.fantasypoints.com/media/discord) to see our staff's wagers as soon as we make them!

#### __Historical Hints__

The favorite has led the league in receiving yards three times in the last decade, with __Justin Jefferson__ (+800) last doing it in 2022. __Jaxon Smith-Njigba__ (+3000) and __Ja’Marr Chase__ (+900) joined Jefferson as league leaders in receiving yards at the age of 24 or younger in three of the last four seasons. Receivers in their age-26 to age-29 seasons were the previous sweet spot to lead the league in receiving yards. No receiver in his 30s has recorded the most receiving yards in the last decade.

Receivers ranked in the top four in odds have led the league in receiving yards six times in the last decade, and JSN ended a three-year run of players ranked inside the top four in odds to win the receiving yards crown. A pace of at least 100 yards per game has been needed to lead the league in seven of the last eight years. __Stefon Diggs__ was the lone exception in 2020 when he led the league at the longest odds (+5000) of the last decade.

Brolley’s Leans
---------------

##### __{{Puka Nacua|WR|LAR}}__ (LAR) most regular season receiving yards (+550, DraftKings)

+ __Why I like Nacau__: Puka is the deserving favorite in this market based on our projections, which place him comfortably ahead of his top competitors. He’s more than 150+ yards clear of the next closest receiver, Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Ja’Marr Chase and Amon-Ra St. Brown are the only other receivers projected at 1200+ yards or higher. Puka ranks behind only Justin Jefferson in career receiving yards through three seasons with 4191, and he’s the all-time leader in receiving YPG with 95.3. Nacua led all receivers in YPG (107.2), receptions (129), TPRR (.37), and YPRR (3.85). Sportsbooks have yet to post odds for record-breaking performances this summer, but Calvin Johnson [made Nacua the favorite](https://www.espn.co.uk/nfl/story/_/id/49078087/calvin-johnson-sees-puka-nacua-top-threat-receiving-mark) to break his NFL single-season receiving yards mark in the near future.

+ __Why I ultimately passed__: There’s not enough value at Puka’s current odds, but there’s a chance that could change once more sportsbooks open this market. I’d be willing to bet on Nacua if +800 odds or longer ever become available. He’s dealt with various nicks and bruises early in his career because of his physical playing style, inviting and dishing out contact instead of stepping out of bounds or going to the turf. His physicality led to some missed time and a 73.6% route share over the last two seasons, which ranked 52nd at the position, behind Andrei Iosivas and Ricky Pearsall. Nacua is also one Matthew Stafford back flare-up away from having Ty Simpson or Stetson Bennett running the show for an extended period of time.

##### __{{Zay Flowers|WR|BAL|23120}}__ (BAL) most regular season receiving yards (+5000, BetMGM)

+ __Why I like Flowers__: The fourth-year WR is popping as a potential wager at his longer odds. He has the 11th-highest projection but checks in with the 15th-shortest odds to lead the league in receiving yards. He’s the clear #1 target for Lamar Jackson after Mark Andrews posted a career-low 24.8 receiving YPG in his first season in his 30s. The Ravens let Isaiah Likely and DeAndre Hopkins leave this offseason, replacing them with rookies drafted in the third to fifth rounds in a weak overall class. Flowers has seen his target share (27.7%>24.1%>22.7%) and air yards share (35.1%>30%>23.7%) rise in each of his first three seasons, and he finished fourth in the NFL with a 92.1% route share in 2025. He’s also yet to miss a game because of an injury over his first three seasons despite playing at a listed 5’9”, 183 pounds.
+ __Why I ultimately passed__: The Ravens have been one of the most efficient offenses since Flowers joined the team, but they’ve attempted more than 100 fewer passes than the next closest team from 2023-25, averaging just 27.3 attempts/game. Baltimore could throw it more under Declan Doyle, but its efficiency could regress after Todd Monken left for Cleveland. Baltimore’s offense ranked first in yards/play (6.17), fifth in passing success rate (49.6%), and seventh in explosive pass rate (9.1%) over his three seasons as playcaller. Flowers could still face more competition for targets later in the summer since they’re one of the top candidates to sign a free agent WR before the start of the season.

##### __{{Christian Watson|WR|GB|23395}}__ (GB) most regular season receiving yards (+12500, Bet365)

+ __Why I like Watson__: The Packers put their trust in Watson with a contract extension and by thinning out their WR corps, letting Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks leave this offseason. Green Bay [vacated](https://www.4for4.com/2026/preseason/2026-available-targets-and-air-yards-tracker) the fourth-most targets (167) and the fourth-most air yards (1661) while adding only returner Skyy Moore as WR depth. Watson is coming off career-highs in receptions per game (3.5), receiving YPG (61.1), and FPG (13.2, WR17). Watson has been held back by his lack of opportunities, but he’s poised to easily clear his career-bests in route share (68%) and routes/game (22.9), which he set last season. Jordan Love could lean on him even more than he has in the past if Matthew Golden doesn’t take a significant step forward after a rough rookie campaign.
+ __Why I ultimately passed__: Watson has worked on his balky hamstring, but his career has been plagued by injury issues through four seasons. He missed 32.3% of his games (22 of 68) after sitting out the first seven games of last season for an ACL injury he suffered in the 2024 season finale. Watson has been a big-play merchant despite his durability issues, averaging 2.40 YPRR, 17.02 YPR, and 10.11 YPT. The problem is he’s never topped 66 targets or 5.9 targets/game in any season. Green Bay could be forced to throw more because of Josh Jacobs’s legal situation and Micah Parsons’ ACL/meniscus recovery, but they’re unlikely to become a pass-heavy team after attempting the third-fewest passes/game (28.5) over the last two seasons.

##### __{{Luther Burden|WR|CHI|26044}}__ (+12500, Bet365) and __{{Rome Odunze|WR|CHI|24977}}__ (+12500, Bet365) most regular season receiving yards

+ __Why I like Chicago’s WRs__: Caleb Williams took a big step forward in his first season under Ben Johnson. One of these WRs could help him to take another big leap if they become the fourth WR in the last five years to lead the league in receiving yards at 24 years old or younger. There are certainly worse bets than throwing darts on both Burden and Odunze at 125/1, especially after the Bears traded DJ Moore and allowed Olamide Zaccheaus to walk in free agency. Chicago [vacated](https://www.4for4.com/2026/preseason/2026-available-targets-and-air-yards-tracker) the 11th-most targets (155) and the fifth-most air yards (1555) while adding just career special-teamer Kalif Raymond to compete for the #3 WR spot. Burden finished third in YPRR (2.83) and fourth in YAC/REC (7.23) in a limited role as a rookie. Odunze averaged 2.11 YPRR and 67.6 receiving YPG before fracturing his foot in late October and trying to play through the injury for a few weeks.
+ __Why I ultimately passed__: Burden and Odunze are vying with Colston Loveland to be the lead receiver for Williams, but there’s a good chance that no Bears receiver truly separates from the rest of the group. Burden led Chicago with a .26 TPRR, which ranked 18th, and Odunze paced the Bears with a 21.9% target share, which ranked 20th. Williams isn’t guaranteed to take another step forward in his development despite leading the Bears to the Divisional Round. He ranked 30th in accurate throw rate (54.2%), 34th in catchable throw rate (69.4%), and 36th in completion percentage (58.1%) among 38 QBs with 200+ dropbacks last season.

Brolley’s Best Bets
-------------------

{{PAYWALL}}

##### __{{Justin Jefferson|WR|Min|21685}}__ (Min) most regular season receiving yards (+1400, DraftKings)

\>Risk .3 units to win 4.2 units. [Placed June 29](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/brolleys-best-bets-nfl-futures#/).

Jefferson already led the league in receiving yards in 2022, and he’s reached 1400+ yards in his first four healthy seasons before last year’s frustrating campaign. We’re buying the dip on Jefferson in a market where he’s been routinely lined at the top of the board. The longest his odds have been in the last four years were at +800, and his average odds have been around +688 in that span. He barely scraped out his sixth straight 1000-yard season to open his career because of Minnesota’s miserable quarterback play.

He ranked sixth in target share (28.5%) and second in route share (93.5%), but he saw a catchable target just 71.7% of the time from __J.J. McCarthy__ and the rest of the QBs after averaging a 79.9% catchable target rate from 2021-24. Minnesota’s QB play clearly frustrated Jefferson, and it bled into his performance, dropping a career-high 6.5% of his targets after sitting at a 3.5% drop rate from 2021-24. He dipped below 2.00 YPRR for the first time in his career after averaging 2.75 YPRR from 2021-24.

The Vikings signed __Kyler Murray__ to fix their quarterback problem, and __Kevin O’Connell__ could get back to his pass-happy ways with a competent triggerman. His offenses ranked inside the top six in passing YPG and pass rate over expectation every season from 2022-24, before ranking 30th in passing YPG (188.7) and 16th in PROE (.2%) last season. O’Connell aggressively threw the ball with __Sam Darnold__, __Kirk Cousins__, __Josh Dobbs__, and __Nick Mullens__ before the passing game bottomed out under McCarthy. Kyler helped __DeAndre Hopkins__ to finish third in receiving yards in his first season in Arizona. Nuk ranked behind only __Stefon Diggs__ (1535) and __Travis Kelce__ (1416) with 1407 yards during the final 16-game season in 2020, and Jefferson finished just behind him with 1400 yards as a rookie. A hamstring injury forced him to miss seven games in 2023, but he otherwise had perfect attendance in his other five seasons to start his career.

full_text:
In our previous editions of the Fantasy Points Brain Trust this off-season, we’ve put some restrictions on our experts: [favorite redraft rookie](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/brain-trust-2026-favorite-rookie-landing-spots), for example. But for this latest article, we posed a much simpler but much broader question: who is your favorite player to draft in 2026 best ball fantasy drafts? Our staff obviously dug a little bit deeper than just saying __Jahmyr Gibbs__ or __Puka Nacua__, but some familiar and not-so-familiar names make an appearance in this iteration of the Fantasy Points Brain Trust.

\> The __Fantasy Points Brain Trust__ article series will recur throughout the 2026 off-season. Make sure to get all access with a [Fantasy Points subscription](https://www.fantasypoints.com/plans)!

Favorite 2026 Best Ball Pick
----------------------------

##### __Josh Allen__, QB, Buffalo Bills

\> __ADP:__ Round 4, QB1 (Underdog)

Ask your favorite best ball bro what their Josh Allen exposure is. If Josh Allen isn’t one of their top-3 highest-owned QBs, I’m not sure they know what they’re doing. He’s easily the biggest edge pick at the QB position, which is the position that scores the most fantasy points. That becomes crucially important as you need to advance through each round of the tournament to have a chance at the $2M grand prize.

Sure, Allen’s safety, consistency, floor, and median are all great — he’s finished (counting backward) as the QB1, QB2, QB1, QB2, QB1, and QB1 by FPG over the last six fantasy seasons. But that almost pales in comparison to his legitimately unrivaled weekly ceiling — he averages 41.7 FPG over his seven best games over the last three seasons (versus Lamar Jackson’s 34.2 or Patrick Mahomes’ 29.4). He needs to have one of those games only once during the tournament rounds to be a “nearly impossible to advance without player.” And that’s the main point — the only players who offer similar “impossible to win the tournament without them” upside are being drafted in Round 1, and Allen is going late-Round 3/early-Round 4.

But another bonus of drafting Allen is that he also gives you an extra roster spot, because you probably don’t need a QB3 if Allen is who he’s been over the last six years. *__\[Scott Barrett\]__*

##### __Christian Watson__, WR, Green Bay Packers

\> __ADP:__ Late Round 5, WR27 (Underdog)

Watson is coming off career-highs in receptions per game (3.5), receiving YPG (61.1), and FPG (13.2, WR17) after missing the first seven games to recover from an ACL injury. The Packers put their trust in him by extending his contract and thinning out their WR corps, letting Romeo Doubs walk, and trading Dontayvion Wicks. A lack of significant playing opportunities has held Watson back, but he’s poised to easily clear his career-bests in route share (68%) and routes/game (22.9), which he set last season. As Ryan Heath pointed out in his “[Finding the Next JSN](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/finding-the-next-jaxon-smith-njigba-playcaller-tendencies#/)” article, Watson averages 17.5 FPG across 13 career games above a 75% route share.

Green Bay could also be forced to throw more because of Josh Jacobs’s legal situation and Micah Parsons’ ACL/meniscus recovery after ranking in the bottom six of pass attempts in each of the last two seasons. I find myself drafting Tucker Kraft (82, TE5), Jayden Reed (84, WR39), or Matthew Golden (110, WR52) if I miss out on Watson because the market hasn’t fully baked in Green Bay’s more condensed receiving corps and a potential uptick in passing volume.

I’m not in love with the backs available in the mid- to late-fifth round, and Watson is an easy click over Rome Odunze, Carnell Tate, and Brian Thomas, who are being selected around him. Watson has top-12 upside if he stays healthy and the Packers give him the biggest role of his career. *__\[Tom Brolley\]__*

##### __Tee Higgins__, WR, Cincinnati Bengals

\> __ADP:__ Round 3, WR15 (Underdog)

Higgins played 12 games in 2026 with a Joe starting at QB — Burrow or Flacco. In those 12 games, he averaged 13.65 FPG, roughly the equivalent of Chris Olave, who finished at WR9 in Underdog’s half-PPR scoring. It was just the three games with Jake Browning at QB, in which Higgins averaged 5.5 FPG, that dropped him to the WR12. And this is the same guy who finished as the WR4 in the same scoring in 2024. And you’re telling me I can get him in the *third round*? Sign me up.

Earlier this off-season, Ryan Heath [examined the “downfall” of fantasy WR2s in 2025](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2025/ryan-heaths-fantasy-football-takeaways#/), and he unsurprisingly concluded that the heavy-TE formation revolution was a significant factor. But he *also* determined that certain *team*s’ #2 WRs (not to be confused with your fantasy team’s WR2) could be pushed down draft boards as a result of fantasy drafters applying the lessons learned from 2025’s trends across the board. That might be what’s happening with Higgins.

I don’t think the Bengals are sending out any signals this off-season that they’re going to change their stripes — they ran the 2nd-most plays in the NFL last season with 2 or more WR on the field. And even supposing they did, Higgins has one skill that will get him on the field in the most critical of situations — scoring touchdowns. Over the last two seasons, Higgins is 6th among all WRs with 27 end-zone targets, even one ahead of his teammate Ja’Marr Chase. And he’s behind only Davante Adams in the number of those targets converted into TDs (12, to a ridiculous *20* for Adams).

Keep in mind that’s despite Higgins playing just 27 games over that span. Of the WRs in the top 50 of end-zone targets the last two seasons, only Adams, Marvin Harrison Jr. (!!), and Mike Evans average more than Higgins’ 1.0 EZ targets per game (tied with George Pickens).

Higgins’ availability in the third round makes him an appealing option for any build, including starting a draft in an old-school RB-RB fashion. He’ll be one of my most drafted players. *__\[Joe Dolan\]__*

##### __George Kittle__, TE, San Francisco 49ers

\> __ADP:__ Round 11, TE9 (Underdog)

All the league-winning TEs before this have an opportunity cost that can burn you. For Tucker Kraft, Tyler Warren, and Harold Fannin, you have to forgo some solid QBs. For the elite trio of Bowers, McBride, and Loveland, you have to forgo quality RBs and WRs. George Kittle affords you the opportunity to get surplus everywhere.

[Every outlook from the medical community believes Kittle will be healthy for Week 1](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2069963234837201085?s=20) (and likely play in Week 2), so it’s possible you’re getting a top-3 TE at a 5-round discount. Even if he takes three to five weeks to ramp up, your investment at this cost does not signal an every-week must-have player, and you can patchwork TE for a few weeks to get you by.

We haven’t even discussed what Kittle does when he’s on the field, which is nothing short of incredible: top-3 in XFP/RR, FPG, 1D/RR, and Passer Rating when targeted amongst TEs in 2024 AND 2025.

In half-PPR, Kittle scored 15+ FP 42.9% of the time (1st amongst all TEs) and 20+ FP 11.9% (4th, but close with Trey McBride, Brock Bowers, and Travis Kelce amongst TEs) of the time since 2023. Even if you get half that production, it’s worth the cost. *__\[Zain Dhanani\]__*

##### __Michael Pittman__, WR, Pittsburgh Steelers

\> __ADP:__ Round 8, WR45 (Underdog)

Michael Pittman is the perfect possession-type receiver to pair with Aaron Rodgers. Those “9” routes on the outside with DK Metcalf can only take the Steelers so far. We witnessed this in 2025 when Kenneth Gainwell led the Steelers in receptions and was 2nd in targets behind Metcalf. Flat out, this team is desperate for playmakers.

DK Metcalf has eclipsed a 62% catch rate season just once since 2021, while Pittman has had 70%+ catch rate every season since 2021, outside of his broken back season in 2024, where he still had a higher catch rate than DK (63.9% vs 61.1%)

Target competition for Pittman in Indianapolis was also substantially better than the competition in Pittsburgh. Outside of Metcalf, Pat Freiermuth, and the rookie Germie Bernard, there is not much. In Indy, Pittman had to compete with both Josh Downs and Tyler Warren for slot opportunities and targets.

I’d also argue that not enough respect is being put on Mike McCarthy’s ability to run a highly functional offense. Leading up to this season, Pittman has hovered just under 30% slot usage, but what if that number goes up? Even if it doesn’t, Pittsburgh should run a plethora of 12-personnel, increasing target opportunities for both Pittman and Metcalf.

Pittman is available nearly 30 picks after Metcalf. Simply put, I believe the markets are drafting the wrong WR1 in Pittsburgh. *__\[Zach Swails\]__*

##### __Ricky Pearsall__, WR, San Francisco 49ers

\> __ADP:__ Round 9, WR46 (Underdog)

475 drafts deep into best ball season, and Ricky Pearsall sits atop my portfolio with a 27.6% exposure rate. Show me another WR available after Round 8 with a real chance to lead his receiving room in a top-5 projected offense. Show me one who’s also been shot and returned to play within two months. That’s what I thought.

Sure, the injury concerns are legitimate — the PCL strain he dealt with last season wasn’t nothing. But let’s talk about what Pearsall actually did when he was “healthy-ish” across six games: 87.4 Receiving YPG (WR4), 2.75 YPRR (WR4), and 13.6 FPG (WR16). He was also a certified “ASS God” in that span — 0.163 average separation score (WR2) and 23.4% route win rate (WR1). That’s not a fluke.

Then we have the upside opportunities Pearsall can take advantage of with the departures of Jauan Jennings and Kendrick Bourne, who vacated 139 targets. Who's left? George Kittle is coming off an Achilles tear, Mike Evans has had hamstring issues in five straight seasons, and in total, Pearsall’s target competition has an average age of 31.7 years. If Christian McCaffrey eases up on sucking the life force out of his healthy teammates, Pearsall could actually benefit from Evans remaining on the field.

And when the offense is fully healthy — which, granted, is a rare occurrence —it’s one of the [most efficient units](https://x.com/FantasyPtsData/status/2070245398145331403?s=20) in football. On top of that, Brock Purdy has been criminally underrated for years now. Over the last three seasons, he ranks 2nd in ANY/A (7.78), 3rd in CPOE (5.0%), and 5th in catchable throw rate (77.8%). Pearsall couldn’t ask for a better situation if he tried.

Look, I’m not usually one to lean on karma as an analytical tool, but the 49ers have been one of the unluckiest runs over the last few years, and at some point, that luck has to turn. The market is still pricing Pearsall as if he’ll be perpetually injured, and with a WR46 price tag, he’s the single-most exploitable discount pick on the board. *__\[Kyle Menton\]__*

##### __Blake Corum__, RB, Los Angeles Rams

\> __ADP:__ Round 8, RB34 (Underdog)

When you are perfectly executing a robust RB strategy in your best balls drafts, eventually you will need to pivot back to RB after drafting 5 straight WR’s between rounds 3-7. To me, there is no better RB option in this range than Blake Corum, who offers the highest floor and ceiling combination of any RB in this range.

The floor case for Corum is attractive by itself, as he worked his way into a 60-40 rushing split with Kyren Williams by Week 7 through the end of the season last year. Over the final 11 games, Corum posted 116 carries for 590 yards and 5 TDs. Corum’s efficiency metrics (60.3% success rate, 6.9% explosive run rate, 0.19 MTF/ATT, 5.1 YPC) were in line with Kyren Williams (64.0% success rate, 6.1% explosive run rate, 0.19 MTF/ATT, 5.1 YPC) during that stretch as well. That tells me that the backfield split is here to stay, and if Corum is scoring enough to be in my lineup a third of the time, that is an easy pick as the first RB off my bench.

The main reason why I am drafting Corum in the 8th round is the ceiling case. There are exactly two RBs who have rushed for 1100+ yards and 10+ TDs in each of the last three seasons — Derrick Henry and… *Kyren Williams!* Corum is mostly a zero in the passing game, but if Kyren were to go down for any stretch of games, Corum would instantly become a top-5 RB on rushing upside alone.

The Rams are favored in 16 of 17 games this season and have even discussed handing 50% of the run-game duties to Corum. If that number were to spike due to injury, there is not a better pick that you can make at the RB position in the 8th round or later. *__\[Bill O’Brien\]__*
